draft.title: Perspectives
card: A perspective is the way a person sees an event. People in the past saw the same event differently.
Who a person was can shape what they saw. Age, job, wealth, gender and where they lived can all matter.
A source, such as a letter or a diary, is made by one person or group. It shows their point of view and may leave out what others saw.
To understand an event better, historians read sources from different people and compare them.
draft.remember: A source shows one point of view, so compare sources from different people.

a.q: Why can a historian not rely on one diary to understand a past event fully?
opts: It shows one person's view and may leave things out
It must be false because it is old
It only describes events that did not happen
It shows what everyone at the time thought
a.why: A diary is written by one person, so it shows what that person saw and thought. Others may have seen the event differently. Being old does not make a source false.
a.clue: Think about who wrote the diary.

b.q: A shipowner and a sailor both write about a long voyage. The shipowner says it went well, but the sailor describes hunger and hard work. What is the best explanation?
opts: They had different roles, so they saw the voyage differently
One of them must have been lying
The sailor was not on the voyage
The shipowner knew more, so only his view counts
b.why: The shipowner and the sailor had different roles and so noticed different things. Both sources are useful when read together. Nothing says either one lied, and one view does not cancel the other.
b.clue: Compare what each person's job was on the voyage.

a.best: It shows one person's view and may leave things out

b.best: They had different roles, so they saw the voyage differently
